IS : 8750 - 1978 

Indian Standard 

PACKING OF^BOTTOM ROLLERS 
FOR DRAFTING SYSTEMS 



0. FOREWORD 

0.1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards 
Institution on 24 March 1978, after the draft finalized by the Spinning 
Machinery (Cotton System) Sectional Committee had been approved by 
the Textile Division Council* 

0*2 Packaging plays an important part in preventing damage in handling, 

ntnv*<r& onr! tv*s»crwM*i» r\f tvf\t\A<z Pmnpr r*ar*lrrnytn & With fc*t1Krfr*^tnrv 

quality of packing materials protects the goods from hazards of transit 
and provides ease of handling This code gives detailed procedure for 
inland B.ndi export ^ackin** of bottom rollers* 



1. SCOPE 

1,1 This standard specifies detailed procedure for packing of bottom 
rollers for drafting systems ( for requirements of bottom rollers, see 
IS t 2510-1976* )« It covers both inland and export packing of rollers. 

2. NOMENCLATURE 

2*1 For the purpose of this standard, the nomenclature used in IS: 2510* 
1976* shall be followed. 

3. INLAND PACKING 

3.1 The rollers shall be properly oiled with anti-rust oil before packing. 
Effective life of such oil should not be less than six months* 

3.2 All the lines shall be packed in one case or individual rollers in 
separate cases according to the convenience and facilities available with 
the manufacturer. 

3*3 For the convenience of packing, the roller lines may be split up 
either in single or double box lengths. 



^Specification for bottom rollers for drafting systems ( third revision ) t 

3 



IS t 8750 - 1978 

3*4 The packing cases for the rollers shall be manufactured as illustrated 
in Fig* 1. The timber used for manufacture of the packing cases shall 
be any of the species given in Appendix A. 

3*5 Individual rollers shall be packed in polyethylene sleeves sealed at 
both ends or wrapped in waxed paper* These rollers shall then be 
packed in wooden case according to the method given in 3*6 or 3,7. 

3*6 Individual rollers should be fixed in position in wooden blocks 
provided with semi-circular holes ( see Fig, 2 } and placed one above the 
other as shown in Fig. 3. The rollers should be placed on these blocks in 
such a manner that the plain boss of the roller is supported by them. In 
addition to the two supports provided near the ends of the case 
additional support(s) shall be provided for two box length rollers. In 
case of rollers wrapped in waxed paper, the packing case shall be lined 
from inside with plastic or cellophane sheets and after packing the 
material > these sheets should be sealed to form a total enclosure for the 
contents of the case* 

3*7 Two cardboard bushes in case of single box length and three in case 
of double box length should be fitted on the rollers as shown in Fig, 4 
to prevent rubbing of rollers against each other during transportation. 
The bushes should have outside diameter 12 to 15 mm more than the 
inside diameter and width approximately 40 mm- In case of rollers 
wrapped in waxed paper, the packing case shall be lined from inside with 
plastic or cellophane sheets and after packing the material^ these sheets 
should be sealed to form a total enclosure for the contents of the case. 

4. EXPORT FAGKING 

4*1 The roHers shall be packed in accordance with the method given 
in 3.1 to 3*7. However, the individual rollers shall be packed in 
polyethylene sleeves only and not wrapped in waxed paper. The case 
containing the rollers shall be lined from inside with plastic or cellophane 
sheets and after packing the material, these sheets should be sealed to 
form a total enclosure for the contents of the case, 

5* MARKING 

5*1 All cases should be marked with the following; 

a) Consignee's name or initials; 

b) Destination; 

c) Serial number of the consignment; 

d) Manufacturer's name, initials or trade-mark; 

e) Number and type of the lines packed in the case; 

f ) Country of origin, if required; and 

g) Any other information required by the buyer or by the law in 
force.
